name: Splashery lane loop
description: How one Splashery lane runs from the owner's approved queue to the public site (the owner's rules of September 29, 2026). The Operator starts a worker on the lane's assigned model; the worker builds, the full test run and the Operator's clip review send it back until the work is right. Work behind the labs switch, Ops PRs and additive engine PRs are merged by the Operator once the full test run passes: nothing the public sees changes, and a revert undoes it, so the graph treats those merges as reversible. Changes to toys the public already sees wait for the owner's good marks, and going public is the owner's decision alone: those two steps are the irreversible ones, and each sits behind a human gate.
goal: Every lane's work reaches main tested and reviewed, and reaches the public only with the owner's approval.

nodes.name: Operator: brief and start
nodes.brief: Take the next lane from the owner's approved queue (ROADMAP.md, WORKSTREAMS.md). Write its brief, its owned files, branch and PR title, and its review-page record. Start the worker on the lane's assigned model (Opus 5.5 for the engine, toys, sounds and fidelity; Sonnet 5.5 for Worlds content, Studio converters and docs), at most 8 workers at once, paced by the 5-hour limit. Check every worker hourly, including its model.
outputs: the lane's record on the Effect review page

nodes.name: Worker builds the lane
nodes.brief: Build the lane's toys, tools or engine change in the files the brief says it owns, and nothing else. Post a clip of every effect at phone size on the Effect review page, keep the handoff file current, push every hour and keep one draft PR mergeable with main. Never merge.
outputs: the clips and cards on the Effect review page

check.run: main plus the PR, then: npx playwright test
check.pass: every test passes; a failure that also fails on main alone is fixed in its own Ops PR first

nodes.name: Operator reviews clips and diff
nodes.brief: Watch every clip as motion at phone size against the effect quality rules, and read the diff for work outside the lane's files, engine changes that aren't additive, and the locked laptop. Emit fail with notes to send it back; otherwise emit labs when everything is behind the labs switch or is an Ops or additive engine PR, and public when it changes toys the public already sees.
outputs: REVIEW.md: the verdict and the notes

nodes.name: Owner marks the public clips
nodes.prompt: These changes touch toys the public already sees. Mark each clip on the Effect review page: good, or fix with a note.

nodes.name: Operator merges (labs, Ops, engine)
nodes.brief: Merge the PR with a merge commit, once, only when the full test run passed on main with it and it is behind the labs switch, an Ops PR, or an additive engine PR. Then do the upkeep: the docs, the Help and Sound Boards, the lab notebook, and the next lane from the queue.

nodes.name: Operator merges a public change
nodes.brief: Merge the PR with a merge commit, once, after the owner marked every clip good and the full test run passed. Then do the upkeep.

nodes.name: Owner: leave labs?
nodes.prompt: The owner has tried the new toys on his phone with ?labs=1. Should they leave the labs switch and go public?

nodes.name: Operator takes it out of labs
nodes.brief: In a small Ops PR, take exactly the toys the owner named out of the labs switch, and merge it once the full test run passes.
outputs: the Ops PR and its merge

bar.name: The effect quality rules and a green run

inspects.ref: the clips on the Effect review page

bar.acceptance: Every clip meets the effect quality rules at phone size, the full test run passes on main with the PR, and for toys the public already sees, the owner marked every card good.
bar.aspiration: People don't realize they're looking at splats.
